profile.campus: Austin, Travis County, Texas (CyrusOne AUS2 building)
profile.reading:
Per a datacenterHawk listing dedicated to the AUS2 site code, corroborated by CyrusOne's own AUS2-AUS3 campus page, this building sits at 7301 Metropolis Drive, Austin, TX, on the shared 242,000 sq ft / 19MW AUS2-AUS3 campus.

CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten; the company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for $525 million in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it for approximately $15 billion. The Dallas-Fort Worth metro is anchored by CyrusOne's Carrollton (DFW1) facility, which Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry describes the company itself calling the largest data center in Texas when it opened in 2012, and today spans additional DFW-numbered buildings in Allen and Lewisville; Texas's absence of a state corporate income tax and its position as a major interstate fiber crossroads have helped make the state, alongside Northern Virginia, one of CyrusOne's largest concentrations of US facilities.

In 2016, CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease, a transaction illustrating the sale-leaseback and anchor-tenant financing structures common among large colocation operators. Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued to expand its US footprint, including the January 2025 groundbreaking of a new fifth San Antonio campus (SAT5-SAT6) representing roughly $1 billion in cumulative San Antonio capital investment per the company's own materials, indicating continued growth investment in Texas markets under private ownership rather than a slowdown following the take-private transaction.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Austin Data Center II is a 242,000 square foot facility at 7301 Metropolis Drive in Travis County. The operator publishes no individual power capacity figure for this building; the campus as a whole, combining Austin Data Center II and a neighboring facility, is rated at 19 MW total IT capacity. This is not enough information to estimate the number of racks or accelerators this specific building could house.

The facility holds certifications for security audit compliance, payment card data handling, healthcare data, information security management, and US government workload standards, each qualifying it to host corresponding regulated compute. Austin Data Center II ranks nineteenth among the 18 facilities in Texas that publish any power capacity figure, though most of Texas's 133 mapped data centers report no capacity at all. The state's published total is 468 MW, meaning this campus's parent figure represents 4 percent of disclosed capacity in Texas.

Without individual metering published for this building, it cannot be assessed as a constraint on AI scaling or weighted against other sites in the state. The address confirmation places it on a known tech corridor, but no information is published about power delivery infrastructure, water availability, grid interconnect, or current utilization, which would be required to evaluate whether this campus matters to the timing or feasibility of additional AI deployment in Texas.
